WELL.one_line: Owns senior housing real estate operated by top platforms (SHOP), riding an accelerating 80+ demographic wave.
WELL.reason: 39% revenue growth and 43% forward EPS growth are real (occupancy recovery plus accretive deals), and the multi-year demographic runway is unusually visible; valuation is very rich (74x NTM) but not obviously disconnected from the growth path.
sources: Welltower investor updates on SHOP occupancy/NOI trends

VICI.one_line: Owns irreplaceable Las Vegas Strip and regional casino real estate under long CPI-linked triple-net leases.
VICI.reason: 8x NTM P/E with a 7.7% yield and high-teens revenue growth is a rare combination for an investment-grade landlord; main risk is tenant concentration (Caesars/MGM) rather than the real estate itself.

PLD.one_line: Largest global logistics/warehouse REIT with infill-location scale that is very hard to replicate.
PLD.reason: The -26% EPS print is lapping one-time development/promote gains, not a demand collapse; revenue still grew 12%, and post-2023-25 supply glut is thinning into 2026-27, supporting re-acceleration.

red_flags: Sunbelt apartment supply glut (Austin/DFW/Phoenix/Nashville) still pressuring same-store rent growth
CPT.one_line: Sunbelt apartment REIT hit by the 2023-26 multifamily supply wave in its core Texas/Southeast markets.
CPT.reason: Flat revenue and a 69x optically-inflated NTM P/E (small EPS base) with no near-term catalyst; oversupply needs another 12-18 months to clear before rent growth reaccelerates.

ESS.one_line: West Coast (CA/WA) apartment REIT protected by regulatory/geographic barriers to new supply.
ESS.reason: Growth is modest but far steadier than Sunbelt peers because California entitlement friction caps new supply; full valuation but not stretched given the defensiveness.

red_flags: Sunbelt apartment supply glut, same as CPT
MAA.one_line: Sunbelt-focused apartment REIT facing the same regional oversupply overhang as Camden.
MAA.reason: Metrics are marginally better than CPT (positive revenue growth, higher FCF yield) but the structural supply overhang is identical and there is no differentiated catalyst to prioritize it now.

red_flags: Could not identify or verify "Vivmark Residential" as an existing, covered multifamily REIT; a $47.6bn market cap in this sub-industry with a 0% dividend yield is inconsistent with known players (largest peers AVB/EQR are smaller) and with REIT payout requirements
VMRK.one_line: Data-card entry for a multifamily REIT that could not be corroborated against known public filings or coverage.
VMRK.reason: Unable to verify company identity, filings, or business description with available tools this session; treating as an unresolved data-quality flag rather than advancing on unverifiable numbers.

red_flags: reported zero public-biotech leasing in a quarter for the first time in company history
ARE.one_line: Life-science lab-office REIT caught in the multi-year biotech-tenant downturn and office/lab oversupply.
ARE.reason: Confirmed disqualifying red flags: a large dividend cut, collapsing biotech leasing demand, negative profitability, and elevated leverage into large 2026 lease expirations in Boston/Bay Area/San Diego with 6-24 month downtime risk.
sources: Simply Wall St / Equibles coverage of ARE dividend reset and leasing strains, 2026

red_flags: 9.8x net debt/EBITDA, the highest leverage in the office subsector here
BXP.one_line: Premier trophy-office landlord (Boston/NYC/SF/DC) with a growing life-science conversion pipeline.
BXP.reason: Best-in-class assets, but office demand is still recovering unevenly and leverage is elevated versus peers; not a clear enough case yet to prioritize over cleaner names.

red_flags: negative FCF yield from data-center capex ramp
IRM.one_line: Records-storage REIT (very sticky legacy cash flows) diversifying into data centers and asset-lifecycle management.
IRM.reason: 18.5% revenue growth with a real second growth engine (digital/data centers) layered on an annuity-like legacy business; valuation (42x NTM) is full but growth is broad-based, not a one-off.

CBRE.one_line: Largest global commercial real estate services firm (brokerage, outsourcing, investment management).
CBRE.reason: 15% revenue growth, 16% ROE and low leverage at only 15x NTM P/E is a statistically compelling combination as commercial real estate transaction volumes recover.

red_flags: multi-year history of Homes.com cash burn (~$3bn cumulative) with breakeven not guided until 2029-30; capital-allocation credibility still being rebuilt
CSGP.one_line: Near-monopoly commercial real estate data/analytics platform (47% core margins) funding a residential portal war with Zillow.
CSGP.reason: After activist pressure (Third Point, D.E. Shaw) forced management to cut Homes.com spend by $300m for 2026 and guide 2026 adjusted EBITDA to $740-800m (+83% y/y), the stock is at a 7-year low pricing in the burn without much credit for the inflection; core moat is intact.
sources: CoStar Group FY2026/medium-term outlook press release, Jan 2026
TIKR/Motley Fool coverage of CoStar undervaluation and Homes.com spend cuts, 2026

KIM.one_line: Grocery-anchored shopping-center REIT with a defensive but essentially flat growth profile.
KIM.reason: Solid, unremarkable: 26x P/E for ~2% forward EPS growth and higher leverage (6.1x) than better-positioned peers like Regency; not differentiated enough to prioritize.

O.one_line: "The Monthly Dividend Company" — diversified, investment-grade triple-net retail REIT.
O.reason: Growth is modest, but the quality/safety premium (36x NTM P/E, 5.8% yield, decades of dividend increases) is fairly, not excessively, priced; a legitimate income-anchor holding worth the full diligence pass.

REG.one_line: Grocery-anchored shopping-center REIT with low leverage and resuming same-store growth.
REG.reason: Better-positioned than KIM on both leverage (4.6x vs 6.1x) and revenue growth (8.9% vs 4.9%); the -15% EPS print looks like a prior-period comp/gain effect rather than a demand problem.

SPG.one_line: Premier US mall/outlet REIT with best-in-class occupancy and re-leasing spreads.
SPG.reason: Q2 2026 results confirm real strength (real-estate FFO +7.9% y/y, 96% occupancy, raised full-year guidance, and bankrupt Saks Off Fifth space re-let at ~2.4x prior rent) — the data card's -52% EPS figure is a one-time-gain comp distortion, not a growth problem.
sources: Simon Property Group Q2 2026 earnings release/call, Aug 2026

EXR.one_line: Largest US self-storage operator (post Life Storage merger) with scale-driven cost/marketing advantages.
EXR.reason: Growth is soft in the post-2023-25 storage-rate correction, but the platform is the clear scale leader and is reasonably, not expensively, priced for a cyclical trough that should ease as housing turnover normalizes.

red_flags: prior v1 pass already flagged valuation as excessive despite a favorable model rank
growing state-level political/regulatory pushback on institutional single-family-rental ownership
INVH.one_line: Institutional single-family-rental operator/owner facing rising supply competition and regulatory scrutiny.
INVH.reason: 36x NTM P/E on decelerating EPS is rich relative to a business now facing both new build-to-rent supply and a real (if uncertain-timing) regulatory overhang on corporate SFR ownership; agree with the prior excessive-valuation call.

AMT.one_line: Largest global multi-tenant tower REIT, now prioritizing capital discipline over international expansion.
AMT.reason: 34% ROE and a reasonable 24x NTM P/E for a name that has been actively deleveraging and pruning lower-return international exposure (e.g., India); mild EPS deceleration looks like comp noise, not a demand problem.

red_flags: still working through a leveraged balance sheet transition; historical CEO turnover/governance churn
CCI.one_line: Now a pure-play US tower REIT after closing an $8.4bn sale of its fiber and small-cell businesses.
CCI.reason: The May 2026 divestiture (proceeds funding >$7bn debt paydown plus a $1bn buyback) is a genuine, completed de-risking catalyst forced by activist pressure (Elliott); the -4.9% revenue print is divestiture noise, not organic decline, and the 6.3% yield/39% street upside look attractive post-simplification.
sources: Crown Castle press release on fiber/small-cell sale closing and capital allocation, May 2026
Wireless Estimator/DCD coverage of CCI pure-play tower pivot, 2026

red_flags: 8.1x leverage, the highest among the tower names in this batch
SBAC.one_line: Smaller US/Latin America tower REIT with a decelerating forward EPS trajectory.
SBAC.reason: Reasonably priced but weaker growth and higher leverage than AMT/CCI in the same triage batch, with no differentiated catalyst to prioritize it over those two.

red_flags: near-zero FCF yield (0.1%) at the current point in the housing/lumber cycle
WY.one_line: Timberland REIT and wood-products maker, earnings tied closely to housing starts and repair/remodel demand.
WY.reason: The highest street-target upside in the batch (55%) reflects optionality on a housing-cycle recovery, but current cash generation is very thin; better as a watch item for a rate-cut/housing inflection than an immediate full-diligence priority.

AEP.one_line: Large multi-state regulated utility with outsized data-center/electrification load growth in Ohio/Indiana/Texas.
AEP.reason: 19% forward EPS growth is well above typical regulated-utility rates, driven by a real rate-base capex tailwind from hyperscaler data-center demand in its territory; 18x NTM P/E is fair, not excessive, for that growth rate.

CEG.one_line: Largest US nuclear generation fleet, now the premier merchant supplier of firm carbon-free power to AI data centers.
CEG.reason: Confirmed 20-year PPAs with Microsoft (Three Mile Island Unit 1 restart) and Meta (Clinton plant) lock in multi-decade contracted growth at premium pricing; lowest leverage (3.0x) in the batch and a 20x NTM P/E look reasonable against that growth visibility despite a 12-month pullback.
sources: TechTarget/DCD/about.fb.com coverage of Constellation-Microsoft and Constellation-Meta nuclear PPAs, 2026

DUK.one_line: Large diversified regulated utility across the Carolinas, Florida and the Midwest.
DUK.reason: Steady, unspectacular growth but one of the cheapest large-cap utility valuations here (16x NTM) with a growing Carolinas data-center demand pipeline; low risk, reasonable price.

ES.one_line: New England (CT/MA/NH) pure-play T&D utility, cleaned up after exiting offshore wind investments.
ES.reason: Cheapest utility valuation in the batch (13x NTM) with positive FCF yield (rare for the group) and a de-risked, simpler regulated-only story following its 2023-24 offshore-wind divestitures.

ETR.one_line: Gulf Coast utility (LA/MS/TX/AR) with major industrial and hyperscaler data-center load growth, notably in Louisiana.
ETR.reason: 30% forward EPS growth and 17% one-year momentum reflect real, contracted capex growth tied to large data-center build announcements on its grid; valuation premium to peers (20x NTM) looks justified by that growth.

EVRG.one_line: Kansas/Missouri regulated utility with solid but unremarkable fundamentals.
EVRG.reason: Fair value for fair growth (9.3% ROE, below the group's better names) with a less pronounced data-center demand story than AEP/ETR/DUK/LNT; nothing disqualifying but nothing that earns priority over stronger peers in this batch.

EXC.one_line: Pure T&D utility holding company (ComEd/PECO/BGE/Pepco) since spinning off its generation business as Constellation.
EXC.reason: Cheapest large-cap utility P/E in the batch (13.5x NTM) for a simple, low-risk regulated-wires model with some spillover data-center demand near its Mid-Atlantic territories.

red_flags: legacy 2020 HB6 bribery/corruption scandal (Ohio) — resolved via deferred prosecution agreement, fine, and management turnover several years ago, but a governance scar worth re-checking in full diligence
FE.one_line: Ohio/Pennsylvania/NJ/WV regulated utility rebuilding credibility after a settled bribery scandal, with a strong forward growth print.
FE.reason: 58% forward EPS growth and a cheap 15x NTM P/E stand out, and the governance issue is legacy/settled rather than active; still worth flagging for a fresh governance/rate-case check in full diligence.

LNT.one_line: Iowa/Wisconsin regulated utility benefiting from heavy hyperscaler data-center buildout in Iowa.
LNT.reason: 11% ROE (best among the Midwest utility peers here) plus a genuine data-center demand tailwind (Microsoft/Meta/Google all have large Iowa data centers on its grid) supports the growth case at a fair 18x NTM P/E.
